How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
IP: 192.120.45.67
API name: get information of an interface
Parameter_fabricName: Network1
Parameter_nodeId: 12
Parameter_podId: 10
Parameter_interfaceType: Ethernet
Parameter_infoType: Speed

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Send a GET request to retrieve specified information for an interface from a network telemetry API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL endpoint to send the GET request to. This should include the base path without query parameters, e.g., 'https://{ip}/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo'.

params.description: The query parameters for the request.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit nodes pertaining to.

nodeId.description: The node identifier to limit results pertaining to.

podId.description: The pod identifier to limit results pertaining to.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit results pertaining to.

infoType.description: The type of information requested for the interface.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide for building the **GET** request that pulls interface information from a Cisco Nexus Dashboard (ND) instance.  
The example uses the exact values you supplied:

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **fabricName** | `Network1` |
| **nodeId** | `12` |
| **podId** | `10` |
| **interfaceType** | `ethernet` (note the lower‑case value required by the API) |
| **infoType** | `Speed` (capital “S” as defined in the spec) |

---

## 1.  Endpoint

```
https://<ND‑IP>/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo
```

Replace `<ND‑IP>` with your actual IP address (`192.120.45.67`).

---

## 2.  Query String

```
?fabricName=Network1
&nodeId=12
&podId=10
&interfaceType=ethernet
&infoType=Speed
```

Putting it all together:

```
https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=ethernet&infoType=Speed
```

---

## 3.  Authentication

ND APIs are typically protected with a bearer token (or basic auth).  
Add the header:

```
Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_TOKEN>
```

If you’re using a self‑signed certificate, you may need to skip verification (`-k` in curl or `verify=False` in Python).

---

## 4.  Example Calls

### a)  `curl`

```bash
curl -k -X GET \
  "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=ethernet&infoType=Speed" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_TOKEN>"
```

### b)  Python (`requests`)

```python
import requests

url = "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo"
params = {
    "fabricName": "Network1",
    "nodeId": 12,
    "podId": 10,
    "interfaceType": "ethernet",
    "infoType": "Speed"
}
headers = {
    "Authorization": "Bearer <YOUR_TOKEN>"
}

response = requests.get(url, params=params, headers=headers, verify=False)
print(response.status_code)
print(response.json())
```

---

## 5.  Using the Provided Tool

If you want to let the system call the API for you, you can invoke the `requests_get` function like this:

```json
{
  "url": "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo",
  "params": {
    "fabricName": "Network1",
    "nodeId": 12,
    "podId": 10,
    "interfaceType": "ethernet",
    "infoType": "Speed"
  }
}
```

(You’ll still need to supply the bearer token in the request headers; the tool’s signature doesn’t expose a header field, so you’d normally add it manually in your own code.)

---

### Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|---|------|
| ✅ | Base URL + endpoint |
| ✅ | Query parameters (exact case) |
| ✅ | Authorization header |
| ✅ | Optional SSL verification flag |
| ✅ | Test with `curl` or Python first |

That’s all you need to generate a RESTful API request to fetch the speed of an Ethernet interface on node 12, pod 10, within fabric “Network1” on your Nexus Dashboard. Happy querying!
